title: The Static App
summary: Serve a personal portfolio site to the world — fast, cheap, and everywhere.
narrative:
You've built a beautiful static portfolio: HTML, CSS, a few images. It works perfectly on your laptop. Now the whole world wants to see it, and a single server on your desk won't cut it.

The challenge is deceptively simple: get static content to visitors anywhere on Earth with low latency, without melting your one origin server every time a link goes viral. The lesson of this level is the single most important trick in web performance — push content to the edge and keep clients away from the origin.

Lay out a delivery path from the visitor's browser, through a content delivery network, back to the server and its asset storage. Get the flow right and the internet feels instant.

functional: Serve HTML, CSS, JS, and images to any visitor
Deliver cached content from a location near the user
Keep the origin server reachable for cache misses
nonFunctional: Survive a traffic spike without overloading the origin
constraints: Visitors must not hit the origin server directly
Static assets live in durable object storage, not on the server disk
capacity: A few GB of static assets
specs.tradeoff: Caching at the edge trades a little content freshness for a massive win in latency and origin load.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring & Alerting so you know when the origin is struggling.

missions.label: Add a CDN to cache content at the edge
Add a Web Server as the origin
Route the Client through the CDN
Let the CDN reach the origin Web Server on a miss

topologyRules.message: Visitors must reach content through the CDN, never straight to the origin Web Server.
Traffic from the Client to the Web Server must pass through the CDN.

resilienceRules.message: A Web Server needs durable object storage (Blob Storage) to hold its static assets.

hints: Every design starts with the Client. Drag it on first, then think about what the request touches next.
The CDN sits between the Client and the origin. Wire Client → CDN → Web Server.
The Web Server reads its files from Blob Storage — connect them so your assets have a durable home.
